Website design for tutors and educators

In short

A tutoring or education website is chosen by a parent on behalf of a student, and trust is the entire purchase. Subjects and year levels, your qualifications and working-with-children check, how sessions run, and what it costs are what a parent checks before making contact.

What comes first

What a tutoring or education business website has to answer, in order.

Not everything matters equally. These four decide whether an enquiry happens, and they belong above everything else on the page.

Subjects and year levels

Specific — 'HSC Chemistry' or 'primary literacy', not 'tutoring'. Parents search exactly what their child needs.

Your credentials and clearances

Teaching qualifications, subject background and a current working-with-children check. For a parent, the clearance is non-negotiable.

How sessions actually run

In person, online, at home, in a centre; one to one or small group; session length and frequency.

What it costs

Per session or per term, and what happens if a session is missed. Tutoring is a recurring commitment and parents budget for it.

How your customers buy

The decision you are actually competing in.

A parent looks for a tutor when a specific problem appears — a bad report, an approaching exam, a child losing confidence. They want reassurance that you have handled this before, that you are safe to be alone with their child, and that the arrangement is manageable. Warmth and specificity both matter.

That is what we design the page order around. The structure follows how the decision gets made, not how the business is organised internally.

Included in every build

  • Keyword-researched copy for this industry, not generic web design text
  • A direct answer near the top that search engines and AI assistants can quote
  • Schema markup matched to what is visible on the page
  • Search Console and Analytics configured before launch
  • A site you can update yourself afterwards

Cost

What affects the cost of a tutoring or education business website?

Scope varies enough within this industry that a single figure would mislead you. These are the decisions that actually move the number.

DecisionWhy it changes the price
Subject and level pagesOne per subject and stage you want enquiries for.
Booking and schedulingRecurring weekly sessions are a real scheduling problem worth solving properly.
Multiple tutorsEach needs a profile with subjects, credentials and clearance.
Online session supportVideo, resource sharing and payment if you teach remotely.
Licensing and compliance

Anyone working with children in Australia requires a state working-with-children check, and parents will look for it. Publish that clearances are held and current for every tutor. Be careful with outcome claims — guaranteeing a result or a band is both unprovable and, in some contexts, misleading conduct.

Questions

What educators ask us.

What should a tutoring website include?
The subjects and year levels you teach, your qualifications and working-with-children clearance, how sessions run, what it costs, and how a parent gets started.
Should we guarantee results?
No. It is unprovable, it attracts the wrong expectations, and depending on how it is worded it can amount to misleading conduct. Describe your approach and let parents judge.
How important is the working-with-children check?
It is the first thing a careful parent looks for. State that every tutor holds a current clearance, and keep it accurate as staff change.
Do we need a page for each subject?
For each subject and stage you want enquiries in, yes. A parent searching 'HSC Maths tutor' will not find you through a general tutoring page.
Should we publish prices?
Yes. Tutoring is a recurring cost and parents will not enquire without knowing whether it fits the household budget. Per-session and per-term pricing both work.
